keys.meta_title: Hearing Test Online: Free Frequency and Ear Check | CoreSkillAI
keys.meta_desc: Free online hearing test with headphones. Find the highest pitch each ear can hear and compare your left and right ear at five frequencies. About 6 minutes.
keys.hea_desc: Find the highest pitch each ear can hear and compare your left and right ear at five frequencies. Headphones needed.
keys.hea_how1: Use wired or Bluetooth headphones, not the speakers. Sit somewhere quiet.
keys.hea_how2: First you set the volume once. Do not change it again until the end.
keys.hea_how3: You will hear short beeps in one ear at a time. After each one, say whether you heard it. Some beeps are silent on purpose.
keys.hea_how4: Takes about 6 minutes. This is a screening for curiosity, not a medical hearing test.
keys.hea_start_desc: Finds the highest pitch each ear can hear and compares how quiet a sound each ear picks up at five pitches.
keys.hea_side_q: Where did you hear the beep?
keys.hea_side_note: Put your headphones on the right way round: R on the right ear.
keys.hea_vol1: Play the tone and adjust your device volume until you hear it clearly but it is not loud. Think of a quiet conversation.
keys.hea_vol2: Do not touch the volume again until the test ends. Stop at once if any tone is uncomfortable.
keys.hea_chart: Quietest tone heard, in dB relative to your volume setting
keys.hea_chart_note: Lower on the chart means a quieter tone was heard.
keys.hea_unrel: You answered "I heard it" to silent trials.
keys.hea_unrel2: The results below are not reliable. Find a quieter place and try again, answering only when you are sure.
keys.hea_range_note: The upper limit of hearing drops with age, starting with the highest pitches. Many headphones and almost all phone speakers also stop reproducing sound somewhere above 15 to 18 kHz, so a tone you did not hear may simply not have been played.
keys.hea_range_low: You heard no tone above 12 kHz with either ear. If that surprises you, check that the volume was not too low, then repeat with other headphones.
keys.hea_sym: Your two ears needed similar levels at every pitch tested. This compares your ears with each other; it cannot say how your hearing compares with other people.
keys.hea_disclaimer: This test runs through uncalibrated headphones, so it reports levels relative to your volume, not in dB HL. It cannot diagnose hearing loss. Sudden hearing loss in one ear is a medical emergency: see a doctor the same day.
keys.hea_noaudio: Your browser cannot play test tones. Try a current version of Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge.
keys.hea_side_both: The beep was in one ear only.
keys.hea_side_wrong: The beep was in the other ear.
keys.hea_side_fix: Check that the headphones are not reversed and that mono audio is off in your accessibility settings, then try again.
keys.hea_asym_r: Your right ear needed a clearly louder tone than your left ear at two or more pitches. That pattern is worth a proper hearing test with an audiologist, especially if it is new or comes with ringing or a blocked feeling.
keys.hea_asym_l: Your left ear needed a clearly louder tone than your right ear at two or more pitches. That pattern is worth a proper hearing test with an audiologist, especially if it is new or comes with ringing or a blocked feeling.
